attacks.claim: Post-cutover rollback is not a clean reversal. The plan re-imports only new Ghost signups to MailPoet, but does not say how unsubscribes, bounces, paid-member status changes, or Stripe subscription changes made in Ghost during the 30-day window are reconciled back. The member lists and billing can diverge.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet." ABSENT: handling of unsubscribes, bounces, and Stripe changes after cutover, and a cutoff after which rollback is no longer viable.

attacks.claim: The success measure of zero send-day outages has no observability plan. Ghost, MySQL, backups, and Mailgun all run on one 8 GB VPS, the same single-point shape that caused the four prior outages, and there is no uptime monitoring, alerting, send-progress tracking, or named on-call owner.
attacks.evidence: "Zero send-day outages over the first quarter." ABSENT: uptime monitoring, health checks, alerting on Ghost/MySQL/Mailgun failures, send-progress monitoring, and an on-call owner.

attacks.claim: The first full send to 46,000 subscribers is irreversible, yet the plan defines no abort, hold, or retry procedure for a mid-send Mailgun batch failure. The go/no-go gate uses only bounce and complaint rates, with no sample size or measurement window, and no editorial or link QA step before the seed send.
attacks.evidence: "First Ghost send goes to a 2,000-subscriber seed segment; the remainder sends 2 hours later if bounce rate < 2% and complaint rate < 0.1%." ABSENT: retry/resume behaviour, abort path, measurement window, minimum sample, and pre-send content/link QA.

attacks.claim: The backup plan is untested for restore. Only the export round-trip is rehearsed; the full MySQL dump, which is the sole copy of the member and consent record on the same box as the app, is never restored. There are no RTO/RPO targets and no alerting when nightly dumps fail.
attacks.evidence: "MySQL 8 on the same box, nightly encrypted dumps to object storage (30-day retention)." ABSENT: full-dump restore drill, RTO/RPO, and failed-backup alerting.

attacks.claim: The 37 paid members with mismatched emails are left to manual resolution with no go/no-go criterion. The plan does not require verifying that every paying member has a live Ghost entitlement and a matching Stripe subscription before cutover, so paying members could lose access or be billed without entitlement.
attacks.evidence: "37 members with mismatched emails were identified in a dry run and will be resolved by hand before cutover." ABSENT: a post-import check that every paid member has a live entitlement, and a fallback for any unmatched member at cutover.

attacks.claim: Double-billing risk is unaddressed. The plan connects Stripe to Ghost but never states that the membership plugin's existing Stripe subscriptions are cancelled or paused, so members could be charged by both systems during the parallel window.
attacks.evidence: "Stripe: existing Stripe account connected directly; no change in processor." ABSENT: halting of billing in the membership and Stripe plugins and duplicate-subscription checks.

attacks.claim: Suppression is asserted but not verified end to end. The plan has a count reconciliation before the production import, but no check that suppressed addresses stay suppressed in Ghost after import, and no protection if the import is re-run.
attacks.evidence: "Unsubscribed and bounced addresses are imported as suppressed (never as active)" and "counts reconciled against MailPoet totals ... before the production import."

attacks.claim: The exit-path rehearsal uses a 50-address list, so it validates the mechanism but not behaviour at 46,000 subscribers, including unsubscribe write-back volume.
attacks.evidence: "In week 2 we rehearse this end to end with a 50-address internal list through Postmark Broadcasts"

attacks.claim: The run-cost figure is approximate and the storage line is unsized. $48 plus $90 is $138 before storage, and export and dump retention sizes are not given. Transition costs (read-only WordPress VPS, staging copy, Postmark rehearsal, warm-up sends) are not budgeted.
attacks.evidence: "Total run cost: ~$140/mo VPS + Mailgun + storage, vs $95/mo today." and "WordPress stays running read-only on the old VPS for 30 days"

attacks.claim: Bulk send spend has no cap or alert. Mailgun bills per recipient, and no volume guard exists for replayed imports, post-rollback re-sends, or a looping unsubscribe write-back.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: Mailgun spend cap, per-send volume limit, or billing alert. "Mailgun ... estimated $90/mo at our volume (46k x ~4.3 sends/month)."

attacks.claim: The timeline has no slack. Week 3 carries the Stripe dry run, reconciliation, training, and a MailPoet send, and week 4 holds cutover and the first Ghost send, so any week-3 slip compresses the cutover window.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: Stripe import dry run, reconciliation, editor training; final Thursday send on MailPoet. Week 4: cutover Tuesday, seeded first send Thursday"

attacks.claim: Redirect and routing changes have no stated rollback, and the URL check covers only the 2,000 most-visited URLs. Broken long-tail paths or bad 301s could affect search indexing, which DNS rollback does not undo.
attacks.evidence: "A crawl of the 2,000 most-visited URLs from analytics must return 200/301 before cutover." ABSENT: routes.yaml rollback and long-tail URL coverage.

attacks.claim: The DNS cutover has no pre-switch health verification or go/no-go gate. The plan lowers TTL a week ahead but does not confirm that resolvers honoured the change or that Ghost is healthy before the switch.
attacks.evidence: "DNS TTL lowered to 300 s one week before cutover." ABSENT: pre-cutover health verification and a go/no-go check.

attacks.claim: The 37 manual Stripe-to-member linkage edits have no recorded pre-change snapshot, so the changes are not clearly reversible.
attacks.evidence: "37 members with mismatched emails ... will be resolved by hand before cutover." ABSENT: pre-change snapshot of member-to-Stripe linkage.
